title: Manager, Engineering, Secure Build and SCS Services (East Coast Preferred)
original_description:
About Docker

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________

Secure Build builds and operates the infrastructure behind Docker's container builds. The team owns Docker Build Cloud and Docker Hub Automated Builds while developing the next generation of trusted build and CI capabilities. Its direction is to make Docker the trusted place CI runs: isolated execution, brokered access to secrets and networks, and verifiable evidence of what each build or test job did. The work spans Go services, container and build technology, cloud infrastructure, sandboxing and software supply-chain security, alongside the operational responsibility for production systems customers already depend on.

SCS Services builds the backend systems and product capabilities that help developers understand, secure and ship software with confidence. The team powers important parts of Docker Scout and Docker Hardened Images, including the services and workflows that turn supply-chain data into useful developer, customer and agent experiences. Its estate is deliberately polyglot, with Clojure and Go services, event-driven workflows, Kafka, legacy Datomic components and newer Spanner-backed services. It also supports the customer journey around discovering, assessing, subscribing to and managing hardened artefacts.

We are looking for one Engineering Manager to lead both teams. Together they sit at the centre of Docker's secure software supply-chain work: one creates trusted build outcomes, while the other turns build, artifact and dependency data into services and experiences used across Scout and Docker Hardened Images. This is a two-team leadership role with separate roadmaps, production responsibilities and technical domains. The teams should deliver independently, with explicit contracts and joined-up ownership where their services connect.

You will own the health, delivery and growth of both teams and make the trade-offs that keep them effective as a portfolio. You will not be expected to be the deepest expert in every language or domain. You will need enough technical breadth and current engineering judgement to engage credibly in designs, reviews and incidents across both teams, set direction with strong senior engineers, and recognise when the right answer is to create space for their expertise.

The kind of person we're looking for

The successful candidate leads first. They are an experienced engineering manager who can inherit two capable teams, earn trust quickly and help each become a high-performing, value-delivering part of the wider Docker organisation. They are deliberate about where they spend their attention, protect both teams from becoming the second priority, and make portfolio trade-offs visible rather than allowing urgency, proximity or the loudest stakeholder to decide.

They stay close to the technical work without trying to own every technical decision. They can hold a substantive conversation about distributed backend systems, event and data pipelines, build and CI infrastructure, trust boundaries and production operations. They are active in design and review, useful during incidents and willing to get hands-on where that moves the work forward. The balance still tilts strongly to leadership, coaching, delivery and organisational judgement.

They care about security as a product and engineering property, not only as compliance. They understand how modern attacks exploit identity, secrets, dependencies and build systems, and they can reason about the evidence customers need to trust an artefact or workflow. They lead through judgement, clarity and unblocking rather than ceremony for its own sake. Above all, they grow the engineers around them and help both teams ship outcomes developers and enterprises can rely on.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead Secure Build and SCS Services, owning delivery, team health, growth, performance and operational excellence across both.

  • Turn two changing roadmaps into a coherent portfolio plan with explicit priorities, capacity and trade-offs, and create leadership coverage so neither team becomes the permanent second priority.

  • Partner with Product to shape strategy and roadmaps for secure build, Docker Scout, Docker Hardened Images and the services that connect them.

  • Stay close to the technical work through design and code review, incident response and selective hands-on contribution where it adds leverage.

  • Ensure each team's technical direction supports product, security, reliability and customer priorities, setting it collaboratively with Staff and senior engineers while leaving clear decision ownership with them.

  • Own the interfaces between the teams, including trust boundaries, contracts, data quality, versioning, operational ownership and customer-facing failure modes.

  • Balance new product work with inherited systems and on-call, and invest in reliability improvements driven by recurring operational pain.

  • Own engineer growth and performance, handle difficult conversations directly, hire and retain strong people and build succession depth within both teams.

  • Align Product, Design, Security, DHI Content, Registry, Hub, sales, support, commercial and legal partners while shielding the teams from churn.

  • Lead disciplined use of AI-assisted engineering and communicate decisions, risks and progress clearly across UK and US working hours.

Qualifications

title: Frontend Engineering Lead
original_description:
Our Mission

At Omnea, we’re reinventing how enterprise businesses operate, starting with the most painful parts: procurement – where a single purchase can drag on for months, trigger 50+ emails, and pull in Finance, Legal, Security, and IT just to get something approved.

We’ve raised $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners, and Accel to change that. Our AI-native platform connects every person, step, and system so buying is fast, safe, and efficient – one place to request, automated approvals and renewals, real-time supplier risk, and complete spend visibility.

The opportunity is massive. Every enterprise on the planet has this problem and nobody has solved it. We’ve 10x’d ARR to double-digit millions in 18 months and are trusted by global enterprises like Spotify, MongoDB, Monzo, and Albertsons. We’re now the 4th fastest growing startup in Europe & the Sunday Times' #1 Best Medium Sized Tech Company To Work for.

Our team previously scaled Tessian (cybersecurity tech, backed by Sequoia, Balderton, Accel, acquired post-Series C), and our team includes ex-founders operators who’ve grown unicorns, shipped world-class products, and executed at the highest levels. You’ll work alongside leaders like Ben, Abs, Sabrina, and Rebe.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for a Frontend Lead Engineer to own the front end at Omnea.

Our design system is growing fast, our front-end architecture is becoming more complex, and right now ownership of these things is distributed. You'd be the person who takes this to the next level.

You'll work across every product team. You'll own the design system, own the front-end architecture, and set the standard for how we build interfaces. We're a tight-knit group of ambitious builders who hold the bar high. It took over 10,000 interviews to hire our first 50 Omneans. Over the next year, our engineering team will double in size, our enterprise customer base will grow from ~180 to 300+, and revenue will triple. The front end has to scale with it.

This is a craft role with real leverage. Almost every engineer at Omnea ships front end. What you build determines how well they do it.

Procurement is a harder interface problem than it sounds. Approval workflows that branch and re-route, dense tables people live in all day, intake forms that adapt to what someone is buying. Getting this right is the difference between software people tolerate and software people actually like using.

What Can You Expect On Our Engineering Team?

  • Join a Skilled Team. Become part of one of Europe's fastest-growing software companies, working alongside experienced full-stack product engineers and product designers from top technology businesses and startups.

  • Own the Design System. You'll own our design system outright: components, patterns, tokens, documentation, and adoption. You'll partner closely with Design to turn intent into reusable, high-quality primitives.

  • Own the Front-End Architecture. Deployment strategy, performance, build tooling, and the conventions everyone else follows. You'll set the direction rather than inherit it, working alongside the engineers and designers closest to each surface rather than owning it in isolation.

  • Leverage Across Every Team. You'll work with all of our engineering teams on their most front-end-heavy projects. The work you do multiplies across the whole org.

  • A Real Design Partnership. Every cross-functional team at Omnea has a dedicated Product Manager and Product Designer. You'll be the connective tissue between design intent and what actually ships, and the person designers come to when they want to know what's possible.

  • Work with Modern Technology. TypeScript everywhere, React and Next.js on the front end, and Meticulous for automated visual regression testing, so you can refactor the design system without fear. Behind it sits Postgres and AWS serverless infrastructure (Lambda, DynamoDB, and EventBridge), managed through Pulumi and deployed via GitHub Actions, with Datadog for observability.

  • AI-Native Development. AI is core to how we build. Engineers use Claude Code and agentic workflows every day to write, review, and ship code faster, and our product is itself built on AI agents that automate complex procurement workflows.

  • Continuous Delivery. We deploy small, incremental changes to production multiple times per day, enabling rapid iteration and fast customer feedback loops.

  • Collaboration and Autonomy. We operate as a high-trust team where individuals are expected to take ownership while collaborating closely to solve difficult problems.

  • Customers at the Center. We regularly engage directly with customers to understand their problems, gather feedback, and ensure we're building products that create genuine value.


About You

  • You're deep in React. You've built complex, production React applications and you understand the framework properly, not just the API surface. Rendering behaviour, state, performance, and where things break at scale.

  • You've owned front-end infrastructure. Rendering strategies, build tooling, bundle performance, and the architectural decisions underneath a large application.

  • You've built or owned a design system. Not just consumed one. You've made the calls on component APIs, driven adoption across teams, and dealt with the messy reality of migration and versioning.

  • You have taste. You care how things look and feel, you notice when something is only 90% right, and you can hold a genuine conversation with designers rather than just implementing tickets.

  • You know CSS deeply. Layout, styling architecture, and building interfaces that hold up across breakpoints, themes, and edge cases. You treat accessibility and motion as part of the craft rather than a checklist at the end.

  • You're a strong engineer first. Your depth and your interest sit in the front end, and that's the point of this role. But you're fluent in TypeScript generally and comfortable working beyond the browser when a problem calls for it.

  • You're motivated by impact. You care about what your work actually achieves, not just how it's built. You thrive with the autonomy to make meaningful decisions and take real ownership of outcomes.

  • You're a team builder. You're excited by maximising team performance, whether that means learning from others or taking the time to explain, give feedback, and level up those around you.

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. This role is new. Its shape will be partly yours to define, and you're happy tackling problems without a predefined solution, backed by an experienced team.


Nice-to-Haves

  • You've worked at design-led companies or somewhere with a genuinely high bar for interface quality.

  • You've performed exceptionally at something else, be it academics, sport, or work. You've gone above and beyond the norm.

  • You love engineering. It's more than a job. You've contributed to open source or worked on side projects just because you enjoy it.


Interview Process

Before applying, we strongly encourage you to spend a few minutes in our R&D Candidate Hub. It covers our engineering culture, ways of working, interview process, tech environment, and what it's like to build at Omnea.

title: Engineering Manager
original_description:
About the role

Radiant exists to redefine how AI infrastructure is built and operated at scale. We are creating a vertically integrated AI platform that brings together physical infrastructure, control planes, and cloud-native software to deliver abundance, control, and sovereignty in a world constrained by traditional hyperscaler models.

Our vision is to enable organisations to build, train, and deploy AI at national and global scale without surrendering control over performance, cost, or locality. This requires engineering systems that operate across software, hardware, and physical environments, and that remain reliable as scale and complexity increase.

We are scaling our engineering organisation now. Most of our engineering manager seats are open. You join, shape how the teams work, and grow with them.

As an Engineering Manager, you lead a team building and operating core parts of Radiant's cloud platform. You combine people leadership, technical judgement, delivery ownership and cross-functional collaboration. You work closely with product, infrastructure, SRE, security and other engineering teams.

This is a hands-on leadership role. It focuses on building strong teams, delivering reliable platform capabilities, and creating an environment where engineers do their best work.

The streams

We run engineering as ten streams in three groups. Each stream is a full team of about nine people: principal, senior and mid-level software engineers, an SDET, a DevOps engineer and a platform engineer. Each stream has its own engineering manager.

  • Infrastructure: Compute, Network, Storage, Cluster

  • Platform: Cloud, Infra, Observability, Security

  • AI: Training, Inference

You do not apply for a single stream. We hire strong managers first. Then we agree your stream with you, based on your strengths and interests. Your first stream is a starting point, not a fixed track. Moves between streams are normal here.

Key responsibilities

You lead one stream end to end: people, delivery and production.

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of about nine engineers across platform, infrastructure and distributed systems.

  • Own team execution across planning, prioritisation, delivery, quality and operational readiness.

  • Partner with product to turn priorities into clear technical plans and achievable milestones.

  • Provide technical leadership on architecture, reliability, scalability and engineering trade-offs.

  • Set strong engineering practices for design, testing, observability, documentation and incident learning.

  • Improve team effectiveness through clear ownership, healthy processes and strong cross-team collaboration.

  • Hire, onboard and retain high-performing engineers. Hiring is a large part of the first year. Expect around two hours a day on it.

  • Support career development through regular feedback, coaching and progression planning.

  • Manage technical risk, dependencies and delivery challenges across complex platform initiatives.

  • Bring AI-assisted engineering into daily work, within our guardrails.

  • Build a culture of ownership, pragmatism, operational excellence and continuous improvement.

Attitude comes first

  • Curiosity: you learn new domains fast. GPUs, networks and storage excite you rather than worry you.

  • Candour: you say what you think, with care. You welcome challenge to your own ideas.

  • Builder mindset: much here is not built yet. You enjoy creating the process, not just running it.

  • Pace with standards: you move fast and keep quality high.

  • Generosity: you make the people around you better. You give credit and share what you know.

Your profile

  • Experience leading engineering teams building cloud platforms, infrastructure, developer tooling or distributed systems.

  • A strong technical background. You engage credibly in architecture and design discussions.

  • A good understanding of:

    • Cloud infrastructure: compute, storage, networking, Kubernetes, containers

    • Platform engineering: APIs, automation, IAM, observability, reliability

    • Distributed systems: scaling, consistency, failure handling

    • Engineering operations: incident response, capacity, performance, production ownership

  • Proven experience in people management, hiring, coaching and performance development.

  • Strong delivery and prioritisation skills across competing priorities.

  • Comfort working closely with product and other engineering leaders in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment.

  • The ability to balance technical quality, delivery speed, reliability and team sustainability.

Experience with GPU, HPC or AI infrastructure is a bonus. Nobody has depth in every area above. Tell us which you know and which you want to learn.

What you bring

  • People leadership: you build strong teams and help engineers grow.

  • Technical judgement: you challenge designs and guide trade-offs without owning every implementation detail.

  • Execution: you create clarity and drive complex work to completion.

  • Systems thinking: you understand how platform components and teams fit together.

  • Operational mindset: you care about reliability, maintainability and production quality.

  • Ownership: you take responsibility for both team health and engineering outcomes.

title: Machine Learning Engineer – Lumen Enterprise Models (SWE-focused LLMs)
original_description:
Job title: Machine Learning Engineer – Lumen Enterprise Models (SWE-focused LLMs)

Location: London; full in-office working as default

Start date: ASAP

Reports to: CEO

Compensation: Salary and Equity options available for discussion

Application deadline: 08/11/26 at 23:59 UK time

___________________________________________________________________________

Help train the software engineers of the future

Cosine is building autonomous software-engineering systems for organisations where reliability, security and control matter most.

Our Lumen Enterprise models are designed to work across real codebases. They need to understand unfamiliar architectures, make changes across multiple files, use tools, run tests and produce software that engineers can maintain and trust.

We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to help train and improve these models.

You’ll work across the full training stack, including pre-training, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. This is a truly unique role that will provide exposure across all areas of the model training lifecycle. WE’re looking for someone who is just as happy to profile the training loop, identifying performance bottlenecks and memory leaks, as implementing new RL algorithms.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working close to the model and cares about the quality of the software it produces.

___________________________________________________________________________

The role

You’ll work closely with research, infrastructure and product to answer questions such as:

  • What should Lumen learn next?

  • Which data and environments will teach it most effectively?

  • How should we reward correct, maintainable and useful software?

  • How do we train models to work across large repositories and long contexts?

  • How do we know when a model is genuinely better for engineers?

The models you train will write code, use development tools, run tests and receive feedback from real software-engineering environments. Your work will directly influence how Lumen reasons about code, navigates unfamiliar systems and improves through experience.

___________________________________________________________________________

Why this role matters

The best coding models are not simply the ones that generate plausible code.

They need to understand context, respect existing architecture, use tools effectively, test their work and recover when their first attempt fails. They need to produce changes that work in the real world, not just on a benchmark.

That behaviour has to be trained.

You’ll work directly on the data, environments, rewards and evaluations that shape Lumen’s capabilities. Your work will influence the models used by engineers and enterprise teams working on complex and security-sensitive software systems.

This is an opportunity to work on frontier model training while staying close to a concrete, high-value outcome: building AI that can genuinely do software engineering.

___________________________________________________________________________

What you’ll do

  • Work across the full training lifecycle, running pre-training, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning experiments.

  • Optimize training methods at scale on frontier models.

  • Diagnose and fix performance bottlenecks and communication overhead in distributed training environments.

  • Train models on long-context, multi-file and repository-level tasks.

  • Develop RL and RLVR loops using signals from execution, tests, linters, static analysis and other engineering feedback, turning fresh ideas into scalable, reproducible code.

  • Investigate model failure modes such as poor planning, brittle fixes, reward hacking and regressions.

  • Collaborate with infrastructure, platform and data teams.

___________________________________________________________________________

What we’re looking for

You may come from machine learning research, applied ML, model training or a closely related engineering background.

You should have:

  • Strong experience training deep-learning models in a production or research environment.

  • Deep practical experience with PyTorch or a comparable framework.

  • Experience with distributed training and multi-GPU systems (FSDP, Deepspeed, …)

  • Strong software-engineering fundamentals and a high bar for correctness and maintainability.

  • Clear communication and the ability to explain technical trade-offs.

  • Experience with large language models is important. You should have worked meaningfully on at least one of, pre-training, SFT, preference optimisation, RLHF or RLVR.

We care more about depth of understanding and evidence of strong technical judgement than about having used every tool listed. Even if you don’t tick every box, please consider applying!

A bonus if you have

  • Experience with mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures.

  • Experience with CUDA.

  • Familiarity with vLLM, SGLang or other high-performance inference systems.

  • Experience running jobs on SLURM, Kubernetes or managed GPU platforms.

  • Experience with code-model benchmarks such as SWE-bench, HumanEval or internal repository-level evaluations.

  • Contributions to open-source model-training, RL or evaluation tools.

___________________________________________________________________________

Why join Cosine

  • Direct impact: Your work directly shapes the next generations of Lumen Enterprise SWE models that engineers use every day.

  • Real scale: You’ll work with large, modern open-source models, long context lengths, and multi-node training runs.

  • Full-stack ML engineering: From custom PyTorch code and distributed systems to data curation, RL design and MLOps.

  • Research + pragmatism: You’ll stay close to the latest literature in SFT, and code LLMs, but you’ll be judged by shipped improvements, not just ideas.

If this sounds like a fit, this is a role where you can meaningfully push the frontier of open-source–based software engineering models.

___________________________________________________________________________


Cosine is an equal opportunity employer.


We value diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and ways of thinking, and we’re committed to creating an inclusive and respectful workplace.

We encourage applications from anyone who meets the role requirements, even if you don’t meet every single qualification. If you need reasonable adjustments at any stage of the hiring process, we’re happy to discuss them.

___________________________________________________________________________

Compensation, Benefits & Ways of Working

We’re an in-office team, five days a week, by design. We believe the work we’re doing benefits from being together, collaborating closely, and building shared context.

What you can expect:

  • Competitive salary, benchmarked to the market

  • Equity / share options, so you share in the upside you help create

  • 30 days’ holiday + bank holidays

  • Work hard in the office, collaborate closely, and switch off properly

  • Dog-friendly office — bring your dog to work

  • Weekly team breakfast & lunch

  • Monthly socials

  • Pension

  • High-quality equipment to do your best work

We care about focus, sustainability, and doing great work — not performative overwork. We value people who show up, contribute thoughtfully, collaborate well with their colleagues, and then go home.

This role won’t suit everyone. But if you’re looking for a fast-moving environment, close collaboration, and a team that takes both the work and work-life balance seriously, it’s a great place to be.

___________________________________________________________________________

Agency & Data Protection Notice

To comply with UK GDPR and our internal data-protection and equal-opportunity obligations, we only accept candidate applications and agency submissions via our Applicant Tracking System (ATS). This ensures appropriate privacy notices, lawful processing, auditability, and consistent retention controls.

Any CVs or candidate details received outside the ATS (including via email, Slack, or direct message) will be treated as unsolicited, will not be considered as part of the recruitment process, and will not give rise to any fee or payment obligation.

title: Developer Portal & Community Manager
original_description:
We are the creators of Flipper Zero — a portable device for tech enthusiasts and engineers. It’s a gadget with an awesome community that brings together millions of people around the world.

We’re building a new product — Flipper One. It’s a full-featured ARM-based computer running Linux in a compact form factor, powered by the Rockchip RK3576 SoC.

We’ve decided to make the entire development process completely open and public. That’s why we’re looking for a Developer Portal & Community Manager to own and manage the entire Flipper One Developer Portal: maintaining the wiki, collecting tasks from all development teams, managing all GitHub projects and repositories, and proactively communicating with the community.

This role is perfect for you if you want to be close to the product, see firsthand how it’s built, and help turn that process into a clear and valuable entry point for the community. This is not a “content manager” role — you’ll need to fully understand the development process, track all ongoing tasks, and connect the team with the community to make things happen.

What is the Developer Portal?

The Developer Portal is a public wiki + a set of GitHub projects built around Flipper One. It documents how the project works as a whole, explains the architecture of its major subsystems, and provides contribution guides for the community — showing how people can contribute to each sub-project.

Anyone reading the Developer Portal wiki should come away with a complete understanding of the project structure, each feature, and what exactly we are building.

Requirements:

  • You write clearly, concisely, and without fluff, and can show examples of your work: guides, instructions, READMEs, how-tos, or similar materials

  • Basic understanding of hardware, software, and development workflows (Git, commits, branches, pull requests)

  • Able to explain complex technical topics in simple language and visualize them with flowchart sketches

  • Strong verbal communication skills; you know how to listen, ask precise questions, and quickly extract the key points from chaotic discussions

  • Keep communication with the community productive — without toxicity, unnecessary softness, or bureaucracy

  • Comfortable collaborating closely with engineers and navigating technical contexts

  • Discern useful feedback and constructive disagreement from noise and spam

  • Value structure, logic, clarity, and information quality

  • Genuinely interested in developer-facing products, hardware, documentation, open communities, and the build-in-public approach

  • Proficiency in Russian and English for communication with other departments in the company and the external community

Nice-to-have:

  • Experience in DevRel, technical writing, community operations, or an editorial role

  • Experience working with documentation, wikis, knowledge bases, or developer portals

  • Understanding of the culture of technical communities, open-source, and hardware projects

  • Ability to work across topics at the intersection of interfaces, electronics, product architecture, and internal development

Responsibilites:

  • Own and develop the Flipper One Developer Portal

  • Turn the team’s internal context into clear public documentation, notes, updates, and explanations

  • Join team calls to understand what’s actually happening in the project and maintain a complete picture of it

  • Translate technical discussions into clear, human language without losing meaning or accuracy

  • Moderate community comments, pull requests, and contributions

  • Filter out spam, reduce noise, and keep discussions productive

  • Help users understand how the portal works and how to provide useful feedback

  • Collect signals from the community and bring them back to the team

  • Make sure the portal stays structured, up to date, and genuinely useful

What we offer:

  • Fully remote from anywhere in the world

  • You will be provided with all the necessary equipment for a comfortable working environment

  • Benefits such as VHI, corporate sports, foreign language courses, and therapy sessions

  • A five-day workweek with a flexible start of the working day

title: 3D Reconstruction Research Scientist/Engineer
original_description:
About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About the Role

You’ll join our Research Team in London as a 3D Reconstruction Research Scientist/Engineer — working at both ends of the pipeline, from cutting-edge academic research to shipping directly to customers. Our team builds the reconstruction technology that turns casually captured or domain-specific imagery into high-fidelity 3D reconstructions: everything from Structure-from-Motion through 3D Gaussian Splatting, feed-forward models, and generative models. We’ve shipped 360 splatting to consumers and enterprise customers, developed the splatting tech that runs on phones, and published at CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and SIGGRAPH — more often than not, our papers end up in production.

You’ll work alongside world-class researchers in computer vision, machine learning, graphics, and robotics on large-scale spatial understanding, localization, reconstruction, scene understanding, and geospatial foundation models. This role is open to junior and senior researchers; scope and responsibility are calibrated to your experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Research & Publication — Conduct original research in 3D computer vision, machine learning, and spatial AI; publish findings at top-tier venues including CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and SIGGRAPH.

  • Algorithm Development — Design, implement, and evaluate novel algorithms across 3D reconstruction, neural scene representations, 3D Gaussian Splatting, SfM, meshing, geometric deep learning, feed-forward models, generative models, and spatial foundation models.

  • Research-to-Production — Collaborate with research scientists and engineers to transition promising ideas into customer-facing products — working directly with real capture conditions, real hardware constraints, and real customers on short turnarounds.

  • Large-Scale Experimentation — Build and run large-scale experiments and benchmarking frameworks to rigorously validate and advance new methods.

  • Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration — Partner with world-class researchers in CV, ML, graphics, and robotics to advance large-scale spatial understanding, localization, reconstruction, and geospatial foundation models.

  • Rapid Prototyping — Implement and iterate on state-of-the-art methods for both academic publishing and production deployment, delivering working prototypes to enterprise customers with speed and quality.

What You’ll Bring

  • PhD in Computer Vision, Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or a closely related field — or equivalent demonstrated research experience in industry.

  • A strong research track record in 3D computer vision: reconstruction, depth estimation, novel view synthesis, SfM, SLAM, or closely related areas.

  • A meaningful publication record at top-tier venues (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, SIGGRAPH, NeurIPS, or equivalent).

  • Strong programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch.

  • Evidence that you can carry an idea from research into something real — a shipped feature, a production pipeline, a widely used open-source release, or similar.

  • The independence to drive research projects from idea generation through experimentation, publication, and handoff.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with classical reconstruction tooling (COLMAP or similar).

  • C++ or CUDA experience, and a feel for performance and on-device constraints.

  • Experience with traditional 3D techniques — meshing, texturing, or bringing modern geometry or generative representations into native 3D.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Location & Work Model

This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office.

Inclusive Application

We know the strongest candidates don’t always tick every box. If you’re excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn’t match every qualification listed — you may be exactly who we’re looking for.

Equal Opportunity

Niantic Spatial is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment at Niantic Spatial are considered without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions), marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected category under applicable laws. Niantic Spatial will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with applicable laws. Please contact your recruiter if you want to request an accommodation for the job application or interview process.

Candidate Privacy

I understand that by submitting my job application, the information I provide as part of that application will be used in accordance with Niantic Spatial’s Privacy Notice for Job Applicants and Candidates https://www.nianticspatial.com/applicant-privacy-notice.

title: Engineering Manager - AI Platform
original_description:
Thought Machine's mission is bold – to properly and permanently rid the world's banks of legacy technology. To achieve this, we have developed the foundations of modern banking through core and payments technology which run natively in the cloud. What we are attempting is hard and means we need great people working together to build great technology.

We have grown rapidly in the past few years – growing our team to more than 550 individuals across offices in London, New York, Singapore, Sydney and our newly established Engineering Hub in Lisbon. We have raised more than £500m in funding and our investors include Molten Ventures, Eurazeo, Intesa Sanpaolo, Temasek, Nyca Partners, JPMorgan Chase Strategic Investments, Standard Chartered Ventures, and more.

We have created a culture that enables our team to produce the best work in the industry while ensuring we have fun along the way. We're regularly cited as having a fantastic workplace culture and have been recognised by Sifted magazine as having one of the highest Glassdoor ratings for a UK fintech company and the industry's most generous employee share package. Named one of the world's most innovative fintechs by Global Finance Magazine, we were also recognised by the Financial Times as one of Europe's fastest-growing companies for two consecutive years—and a UK Best Employer for 2026.

Engineering Managers at Thought Machine lead complex technical projects to deliver on our roadmap. To accomplish this you will manage a group of talented engineers as they identify issues and implement creative solutions to address them. You will manage your own project deliverables, contribute to the vision and strategy of your area and help develop and grow your team. We are particularly excited to hear from people who show strong product ownership and enjoy switching between engineering management and being hands-on with technical work.

Your team’s primary mission is to enable everyone in Thought Machine to productively, safely, and easily solve their business problems with AI tooling. You will have a wide remit to design and implement new platforms, adjust pipelines, and introduce new tools when they are the right choice for the job. You will work closely with your team, senior leadership and internal users to define and execute your roadmap.

Duties

  • Actively participating in technical discussions and design reviews.

  • Taking a data driven approach and measuring your team’s impact with the data you can collect directly from your users.

  • Understanding the needs, challenges and impediments of internal teams so you can identify solutions and measure success

  • Contributing to the vision and strategy of your platform area, aligning it with broader engineering and business goals.

  • Contributing to engineering-wide initiatives as part of the engineering management team on anything from recruitment to team processes.

  • Develop engineers in your team and help them in their career development.

  • Leading by example: Code reviews and hands on technical work

  • Championing industry best practices and emerging trends to keep our team ahead of the curve.

Essential

  • 2+ years experience of engineering management in platform teams that include AI tooling and capabilities

  • Experience of working in a cloud-native environment, using modern technology stacks similar to the stack we use at Thought Machine (Kubernetes, AWS/GCP/Azure, golang/python).

  • Technical background to drive technical decisions and great interpersonal skills to drive communication with your users. You should enjoy working in environments where you have a high level of responsibility and autonomy.

  • You are comfortable wearing different Engineering Manager hats that suit the changing needs of a team as it evolves.

  • You have experience developing platforms and tools that are used by other engineers either internally or externally.

Desirable

  • Previously led an AI-first team driving organisational change

  • Experience working in or managing internal platform teams

  • Previously helped recruit and shape brilliant engineering teams.

  • Taken an active role in defining and evaluating effective team processes.

  • Previously worked in a hyper-growth environment.

Benefits

  • Highly competitive salary

  • Pension plan (match up to 5%)

  • Life insurance - three times annual salary

  • Competitive maternity (six months fully paid) and paternity leave (four weeks fully paid)

  • Shared parental leave (matched to our maternity leave for the same point in time)

  • 25 days holiday and bank holidays

  • Flexible working hours

  • Cycle-to-work scheme

  • Electric car scheme

  • Season ticket loan

  • Access to outstanding learning materials and courses

  • Sports and hobby clubs, subsidised by Thought Machine

  • All the latest tech you need

  • Start the day properly with fresh fruit and cereals

  • Huge range of healthy (and not-so-healthy) snacks, smoothies and drinks

  • A talented and experienced team as your colleagues

  • An environment where we encourage learning and progress

  • Two charity days a year

  • Weekly food pop-up

We actively hire candidates who demonstrate technical excellence in their field and welcome people of all ages and backgrounds, providing everyone with equal access to professional development. You are encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't accurately match the job description. We also encourage applications from those with different abilities, including candidates with ADHD, autism, dyslexia or dyspraxia.

You will manage your own project deliverables, contribute to the vision and strategy of your area and help develop and grow your team. We are particularly excited to hear from people who show strong product ownership and enjoy switching between engineering management and being hands-on with technical work. Your team’s primary mission is to enable everyone in Thought Machine to productively, safely, and easily solve their business problems with AI tooling. You will have a wide remit to design and implement new platforms, adjust pipelines, and introduce new tools when they are the right choice for the job. You will work closely with your team, senior leadership and internal users to define and execute your roadmap. Duties Actively participating in technical discussions and design reviews. Taking a data driven approach and measuring your team’s impact with the data you can collect directly from your users. Understanding the needs, challenges and impediments of internal teams so you can identify solutions and measure success Contributing to the vision and strategy of your platform area, aligning it with broader engineering and business goals. Contributing to engineering-wide initiatives as part of the engineering management team on anything from recruitment to team processes. Develop engineers in your team and help them in their career development. Leading by example: Code reviews and hands on technical work Championing industry best practices and emerging trends to keep our team ahead of the curve. Essential 2+ years experience of engineering management in platform teams that include AI tooling and capabilities Experience of working in a cloud-native environment, using modern technology stacks similar to the stack we use at Thought Machine (Kubernetes, AWS/GCP/Azure, golang/python). Technical background to drive technical decisions and great interpersonal skills to drive communication with your users. You should enjoy working in environments where you have a high level of responsibility and autonomy. You are comfortable wearing different Engineering Manager hats that suit the changing needs of a team as it evolves. You have experience developing platforms and tools that are used by other engineers either internally or externally. Desirable Previously led an AI-first team driving organisational change Experience working in or managing internal platform teams Previously helped recruit and shape brilliant engineering teams. Taken an active role in defining and evaluating effective team processes. Previously worked in a hyper-growth environment. title: Tech Lead - Terminals
original_description:
About Ryft

 

Ryft is a regulated payment facilitator and authorised payment institution building the infrastructure layer for modern commerce platforms.

We enable marketplaces, SaaS platforms and multi-party ecosystems to embed and monetise payments natively. Our technology handles onboarding, compliance, orchestration, split payments and revenue sharing, allowing our partners to focus on growth while we manage complexity.

 

We are now entering the next phase of scale, expanding into new verticals and building a category-defining embedded payments platform.

 

About the Job

Are you an engineering leader who wants to own the systems that connect physical point-of-sale hardware to a modern, scalable payments platform?

We are looking for a Tech Lead to head up our Card Present (In-Person Payments) squad. You will lead the technical direction and hands-on delivery of the infrastructure that allows our merchants to take physical payments. You'll work across our C#/.NET backend on AWS, shaping how physical card taps and inserts securely communicate with our event-driven services, split funds, and settle correctly.

This is a hands-on, high-impact leadership role. You won't just be managing a Jira board, you'll be deep in the architecture, writing code, mentoring your squad, and owning the technical strategy for our physical terminal estate. You will bridge the gap between cloud infrastructure and physical hardware, ensuring our in-person payment flows are as robust, scalable, and developer-friendly as our online ones.

What You'll Work On

  • In-person payments architecture: Leading the technical design for our card-present estate, ensuring low-latency, highly reliable communication between physical terminals and our AWS backend.

  • Terminal & Gateway Integration: Building the critical paths that connect smart payment terminals and Point of Sale (POS) systems into Ryft’s core gateway and marketplace routing logic.

  • Hardware-to-cloud flows: Handling the unique complexities of physical payments: offline modes, state synchronization, hardware webhooks, and complex failure modes.

  • Security & Compliance pipelines: Ensuring our physical payment flows remain airtight and fully compliant within heavily regulated environments.

  • Squad Leadership: Setting the technical standard for the Card Present squad. Breaking down complex product requirements into actionable architecture and guiding engineers through delivery.

  • The platform itself: Contributing to our broader event-driven C#/.NET service estate, infrastructure-as-code, and observability tooling alongside other Tech Leads.

Responsibilities

  • Lead technical delivery: Architect, build, and ship end-to-end features for our card-present offering. You are the ultimate technical owner of what your squad ships.

  • Design for hardware-cloud correctness: Write and architect services that behave under network drops, partial failure, and hardware concurrency. Idempotency and absolute accuracy are the job, not edge cases.

  • Raise the bar & mentor: Improve the codebase and our engineering practices. Review code rigorously, set conventions, and level up the engineers in your squad.

  • Own it in production: Take real ownership of what goes live: instrumentation, alerting, and incident response for a system where physical merchants are relying on your uptime to make a living.

  • Harness AI, stay in control: Use AI-assisted workflows to multiply your output (we invest heavily in them) while remaining in full command of every line you ship and review.

  • Collaborate: Work day-to-day with your Engineering Manager, Product Managers, hardware vendors, and other squads to deliver seamless omnichannel payment features.

Experience & Skills Required

  • Technical Leadership: Proven experience leading technical projects, architecting complex backend systems, and guiding small teams of engineers to deliver high-quality software.

  • Strong backend engineering: Significant commercial experience building and running production backend services. Our backend is C#/.NET, so depth there is ideal, but if you're excellent in another modern typed language and will get fluent fast, we want to hear from you.

  • AWS in production: Hands-on experience running distributed services on AWS (ECS/Fargate, Lambda, SNS/SQS, DynamoDB or similar) and understanding the operational reality that comes with them.

  • Distributed systems judgement: Comfortable reasoning about service boundaries, asynchronous messaging, eventual consistency, and building resilient systems that handle downstream provider outages.

  • AI-augmented, engineer-first: You use AI coding tools effectively to move faster, but you review, understand, and take full ownership of the output. We are not looking for someone who ships code they can't explain.

  • Fast, self-directed learner: A track record of getting productive quickly in unfamiliar domains. Enthusiasm to master the complexities of hardware-software interactions matters more to us than knowing it all on day one.

Nice to Have

  • POS & Terminal Integration: Existing experience integrating physical payment terminals, card readers, or Point of Sale (POS) systems into payment gateways.

  • Android Experience: Familiarity with Android development, specifically in the context of building or maintaining applications for smart payment terminals.

  • PCI-DSS & Compliance: Deep understanding of payment scheme rules, PCI-DSS compliance, EMV standards, or Point-to-Point Encryption (P2PE).

  • Infrastructure ownership: Infrastructure-as-code (CloudFormation, CDK, or Terraform), CI/CD pipelines, and containerisation.

Why Ryft? If you want to build the systems that move money in a fast-paced, collaborative environment, we'd love to hear from you. We value engineers who care about the craft, speak up with their ideas, and take pride in what they ship. You'll join a team where your voice is heard, your work matters, and there's plenty of room to grow.

title: Senior Software Engineer (Multiple Teams, Europe)
original_description:
As a Senior Software Engineer on Coder’s Engineering team, you’ll build and evolve the systems behind our agentic development experience. You’ll work across the agent harness, integrations, and workflows that connect agents with real development environments.

You’ll stay hands-on, solve complex technical problems, and work closely with Product, Design, and other engineers to ship reliable agentic experiences.

What you’ll do here

  • Design and build production systems in Go, with work across React and TypeScript where needed.

  • Improve agent execution, tool use, context management, streaming, and long-running workflows.

  • Extend our provider-agnostic architecture as models and capabilities change.

  • Build reliable integrations between agents, workspaces, tools, and developer infrastructure.

  • Own projects from implementation through rollout and iteration.

  • Contribute to design reviews, code reviews, and technical discussions.

  • Partner with Product and Design to turn agent capabilities into useful developer experiences.

  • Improve the reliability, performance, and operability of agentic systems.

What we’re looking for

  • Strong experience building and operating production software systems.

  • Hands-on experience with Go.

  • Experience with React and TypeScript.

  • Experience building systems around LLMs or agentic workflows.

  • Familiarity with model APIs, tool calling, context management, or agent loops.

  • Good understanding of distributed systems and production reliability.

  • Working knowledge of AWS.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and comfort working through technical ambiguity.

  • Someone who contributes beyond their own code through reviews, collaboration, and knowledge sharing.

Bonus tacos if you have

  • Experience building coding agents, developer tools, or cloud development environments.

  • Experience with MCP, agent tools, or multi-agent systems.

  • Experience with remote execution, sandboxing, or isolated compute.

  • Experience building integrations across multiple model providers.

  • Experience with AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, or Linux.

  • Open-source contributions or experience working directly with customers.

Our tech stack

  • Backend: Go, Postgres

  • Frontend: TypeScript, React

  • Infrastructure: AWS, Kubernetes

  • Observability: Prometheus, Grafana

  • CI/CD: GitHub Actions

Coder’s agentic architecture is provider-agnostic. The foundation is built; this role helps extend it, improve it, and ship the next set of agentic capabilities.

About Coder

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com.

Interview process 

We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow. Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders.

AI use during the interview process

As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process.

Not permitted: Using AI assistance during conversational interviews.

Permitted: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.

Our use of AI in hiring

We use AI tools to help manage our recruitment process efficiently and fairly. Specifically:

  • Ashby helps us review inbound applications by surfacing candidates who best match the role requirements we've defined. This tool does not make hiring decisions; it helps our team prioritize which applications to review first.

  • Granola takes notes during our interview calls so our team can focus on the conversation with you.

All hiring decisions are made by humans. Our team reviews applications, conducts interviews, and makes final selections. AI tools assist us but never replace human judgment, and these practices are conducted in compliance with applicable data protection, AI governance, and labor laws. Your data is not used to train AI models.

In accordance with New York City Local Law 144, an independent bias audit has been conducted on "Automated Employment Decision Tools"; results are available for Ashby.

We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, pregnancy, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

title: Software Engineer (Fleet) - London
original_description:
About Us

At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. With thousands of patient rooms across 4 countries already benefiting from our technology, we are aiming to expand to much more. We distinguish ourselves by focusing relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, rapidly deploying solutions that make a real difference.

The Job

Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there.

In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest:

  • Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life.

  • OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward.

  • Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things.

  • Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application.

  • Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely.

  • Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team.

Qualifications:

  • Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs.

  • Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python

  • Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices.

  • Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers.

  • Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards.

  • Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers

  • Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT.

  • Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team.

  • Experience with the NVIDIA Jetson platform and Linux for Tegra is a big plus.

  • Experience with Yocto, Debian packaging, or custom image builds is a plus.

  • Experience in the medical device or healthcare technology field is a plus.

What We Offer

  • Participation in our warrant program (stock options).

  • Work with state-of-the-art technology in a pioneering field.

  • A vibrant, learning-focused work environment.

title: Software Engineer - BYG
original_description:
Software Engineer - Customer Operations Platform

Hybrid in London, UK

We’re looking for a software engineer

iwoca’s operational tools and processes are a competitive advantage, allowing us to give great customer service, manage risk, and get money into our customers’ hands as quickly as possible.

You’ll join our growing Customer Operations Platform team to help improve the systems that power these processes, building tailored flows for our Operations teams, automating processes using AI, using ML models to make smarter decisions, and improving the reliability of our communication services.

You’ll work closely with our Operations teams, getting user feedback and input on requirements from users working in the same building, and seeing the impact of your changes on the people you work with.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The role

As an engineer you’d take whole projects end to end, work out what' s actually needed, design it, build it and look after it in production.

Responsibility and Autonomy:

  • Take on complex projects that span many systems and many stakeholders — e.g. CRM, telephony, contact, and task management

  • Build a strong understanding of the business context: how our ops teams actually work, how the processes you're automating are supposed to run, and what the people relying on your systems need from them.

  • Do the detailed technical scoping and prototyping that tells us whether an idea is feasible before it reaches the roadmap.

Delivery and Collaboration

  • Take on complex coding and architecture problems with a high level of ambiguity and technical complexity.

  • Write fluent technical documents and developer tickets distilling product requirements into clear and actionable technical work.

  • Build relationships with key stakeholders including Operations Strategy, Credit Analysts, Account Managers, and Collections teams.

Learning and Growth:

  • Embody our growth mindset mentality by sharing new technologies and best practices within the team as well as more broadly across the company.

The projects

Here are some of the most recent problems we are solving:

  • iwocaChat. Operations staff spend a large share of their day assembling context from multiple systems before they can help a customer. iwocaChat uses Claude to answer those questions directly, so staff spend their time on the customer rather than the lookup.

  • Migrating the monolith. We are incrementally moving business logic out of our Django monolith into smaller, independently deployable services. Because it cuts across every domain, you'd be shaping service boundaries and ownership models that stick around long after the monolith is gone.

  • Inbox messaging reworking. We are replacing our third party email inbox application with an inhouse solution, utilising AI to enable operations staff to automate the actions of our most frequent customer service enquiries.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Experience developing and owning shared back end services that other engineering teams contribute to and depend on - being the trusted reviewer for their contributions and shaping how they build on top of your work.

  • Familiarity with front-end technologies (React, TypeScript) and browser debugging.

  • Experience building and shaping distributed systems in complex business domains.

  • Ability to translate complex operational needs into technical architecture.

  • Strong capability using AI tools to automate routine tasks and research, enabling greater focus on complex system architecture and critical technical decision-making.

Bonus:

  • Commercial experience with Python frameworks like Django.

  • Experience with complex data architectures, including event-sourced data models.

The salary

We expect to pay from £70,000 - £90,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a brilliant place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Frankfurt, and Berlin with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and clubs, like bingo, comedy nights, yoga classes, football, etc.

The benefits

  • Flexible working.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year, we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Useful links:

  • See iwoca benefits & policies for detail and some additional benefits.

  • See interview welcome pack to learn more about the process.

Compensation: £70K – £90K

  • • £70K – £90K

title: Software Engineer (Frontend) - London
original_description:
About Us

Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.

Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on.

Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We recently raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.

We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.

If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.

The Job

We're looking for an experienced Frontend Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build the features, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Alongside that, you'll help own the quality of how we build: the tests, pipelines and guardrails that let us ship fast without breaking what care teams depend on.

In this role, you will focus on:

  • Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them.

  • Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward.

  • Code Quality & Guardrails: Help own code quality across the frontend. Improve our CI/CD pipelines and automated tests, keep the infrastructure scalable, and build the guardrails that let AI coding agents contribute safely.

  • Backend & APIs: Work with the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them.

  • Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on.

Qualifications

  • Several years of experience building production web applications.

  • Strong TypeScript skills: this is the language for everything we build.

  • Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native.

  • Experience with CI/CD and automated testing, and a strong sense of what good code quality looks like.

  • Great product taste and a keen eye for UX. You work well with designers and can make sensible design decisions yourself when needed.

  • Comfortable talking directly with non-technical users and turning messy feedback into concrete decisions.

  • Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome, from idea to adoption.X

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with React Native and Expo in production.

  • Experience working with AI coding agents in a real codebase.

  • AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience.

  • Familiarity with TanStack, real-time systems or push notifications.

  • Experience with health data or other regulated, privacy-sensitive domains (e.g. GDPR).

What We Offer

  • Participation in our warrant program (stock options).

  • A small team where your decisions directly shape the product.

  • A Copenhagen-based office with close collaboration, no async-only culture.

  • Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate.

Join Our Team

We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job.

At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work.

If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

title: Senior Platform Engineer
original_description:
Attio is the CRM for agentic revenue. Designed for the most ambitious go-to-market teams, it gives companies the power to understand every customer, automate at scale, and build their go-to-market motion exactly as they need. We've raised $116M from some of the world's best investors: GV (Google Ventures), Redpoint, Balderton, Point Nine, and 01A.

We hire builders who thrive on complex technical challenges, hold themselves to a high bar, and genuinely care about delighting the people who use what they build. The team here brings sharp judgement, real craft, and the drive to do exceptional work. We're obsessed about the details and energized by the frontier.

If you want to do the best work of your career, this is the right place.


About the role

Our Engineering team tackles the toughest challenges, so our users never have to. Real-time infrastructure, AI-native architecture, and a frontend that feels effortless - all powered by a team that moves fast, thinks rigorously, and holds an exceptionally high bar for quality.

We're looking for Platform Engineers who treat the platform as a product, with every engineer at Attio as its customer. You'll own the infrastructure, tooling and pipelines that let the rest of engineering ship quickly and safely, and you'll be accountable for keeping all of it reliable, fast and cost-effective as we scale.

What you'll do

  • Build and evolve our platform infrastructure as code (Terraform, Kubernetes, GCP), so every environment is reproducible, version-controlled and auditable.

  • Own our CI/CD pipelines end-to-end, making builds, tests and deploys fast, reliable and secure for every engineer at Attio.

  • Own our observability stack - metrics, logging and distributed tracing - as the foundation of an exceptional reliability culture.

  • Define and hold SLOs for latency, availability and error rates, and manage capacity to stay comfortably inside them.

  • Lead incident response: triage and resolve complex production issues, then run blameless post-mortems and ship the fixes as code.

  • Partner with product engineering teams to remove manual toil and shorten the path from writing code to running it in production.

What you'll bring

  • Hands-on experience operating production systems with an SRE mindset: SLOs, error budgets, toil reduction and blameless post-mortems.

  • Excellent knowledge of modern cloud architectures (either GCP or AWS), including networking, IAM and managed services.

  • Demonstrable deep expertise with Docker and Kubernetes at scale, covering cluster design, networking, storage and security.

  • Proficiency in a modern language such as Typescript, Go, Python or Rust, and a track record of writing well-tested automation.

  • Experience owning mission-critical operational tooling, including centralised logging or APM (e.g. Datadog, Splunk).

  • Ability to communicate technical ideas to the wider team and influence how other engineers build and operate their services.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary of £105,000 to £125,000

  • Equity in an early-stage tech company on an incredible trajectory

  • 25 days holiday plus local public holidays

  • Apple hardware

  • Private medical insurance through AXA

  • Pension contribution through Hargreaves Lansdown

  • Enhanced family leave

  • Team off-site in fun places! (We've been to Barcelona, Lisbon, Malta, and Split so far)

Compensation: £105K – £125K • Offers Equity

  • E3 • Target starting bands, there may be room outside of these decided on a case by case basis £105K – £125K • Offers Equity
